rows.name: Understand brief
rows.summary: What we heard from Pentland and what we will show.
rows.content:
# Understand brief: Pentland Vulnerability Use Case

**Prospect.** Pentland. **Owner.** Gourav Mahunta. **Manager.** Gourav Mahunta.

## What we heard
- Findings arrive from three scanners in separate exports.
- Analysts merge them by hand; critical items wait for days.
- Nobody owns a fix until a ticket is raised by hand.

## What we will show
A ranked remediation queue built from the three exports, with an owner on every item and a manager approval before tickets are raised.

## Out of scope
Corporate IT assets, automatic patching.

## Assumptions to confirm
Retail estate only; about 480 assets in the sample; exports are CSV.

rows.name: PRD with flowchart
rows.summary: PRD v3: remediation flow with the manager approval step.
rows.content:
Pentland Vulnerability Use Case

Product requirements, version 3 · Plan stage · Owner Gourav Mahunta · Manager Gourav Mahunta · In review

What changed in v3. The flow now shows the manager's scan approval before any ticket is raised (judge feedback, round 1). The remediation queue has an owner view next to the triage view (feedback from Gourav Mahunta as manager, round 2).

1. Problem

Pentland's security team receives vulnerability findings from three scanners, each in its own export. Analysts merge them by hand in spreadsheets, so the same asset shows up several times, critical items wait for days, and nobody can say who owns a fix.

2. Goal and success measure

One ranked remediation queue built from the three scanner exports, with a named owner on every item.

MeasureToday (assumed)Target
Time from scanner export to ranked queueAbout 2 daysUnder 15 minutes
Critical findings with a named owner within 1 business dayNot tracked90 percent
Duplicate findings in the queueNot trackedUnder 2 percent

3. Users

RoleWhat they do here
Security analystUploads the scanner exports and checks the ranking
Asset ownerSees only their own items, accepts or disputes them, updates the status
Security managerApproves the scan before any ticket is raised

4. Flow

Step 6 is new in v3. If the manager requests changes, the queue goes back to ranking.

5. Scope

In scope.

  • Scanner exports from three tools, retail estate only
  • Normalise, dedupe and rank
  • Owner review, manager approval, ticket reference stored on the finding

Out of scope.

  • Corporate IT assets
  • Automatic patching
  • Real-time scanning

6. Screens

ScreenPurpose
Upload and scan checkDrop the three exports, see counts per tool and rejected rows
Triage viewRanked queue with severity, asset, owner and status; filters by owner and severity
Owner viewThe signed-in owner's items only, with accept and dispute
ApprovalManager sees the scan summary and approves or requests changes

7. Data

ObjectHolds
FindingTool, CVE, severity, exposure, status, ticket reference
AssetName, business unit, owner
ScanUpload time, counts per tool, approval state

8. Risks and open questions

  • Scanner exports differ in severity scales; a mapping table is needed (assumed one page).
  • Asset ownership may be missing for older assets; unowned items go to the analyst.
  • Which tracker receives the tickets is not decided (open).

All figures are assumptions for review. Nothing here comes from Pentland's systems.
